item.title: Methods for Deriving Nonlinear Kinetic Equations from the Dynamics of Quantum Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.28846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The article outlines key topics related to deriving kinetic equations and, in general, to the relationship between the evolution equations governing quantum many-particle systems. The main issues being considered are the mathematical origin of quantum kinetic equations, novel methods for deriving kinetic equations from hierarchies of evolution equations for quantum systems, specifically focusing on kinetics within the framework of the evolution of observables, and the generalization of the quantum kinetic equation specified by non-separable initial states.
item.dc:creator: V. I. Gerasimenko

item.title: Lieb-Robinson bounds via the Combes-Thomas estimate
item.description: arXiv:2610.28927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies quantum spin systems: networks of spins coupled by local interactions. The Lieb-Robinson bound predicts that in these systems, information propagates at an essentially finite speed. We produce a new proof of this result. Our approach relies on a spectral bound on entries of resolvents of band matrices, the Combes-Thomas estimate, rather than on the standard path-counting argument.
item.dc:creator: Tali Braester, Haochen Luo, George Peykanu, Sergii Solomakha

item.title: On the Road Again: How the $N$-Lane TASEP and Local Reservoirs Drive Jamming in Axonal Transport
item.description: arXiv:2610.28952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intracellular transport by molecular motors along microtubules is essential for cellular function, particularly in neuronal axons where track disruption drives neurodegenerative disease. We develop an \(N\)-track totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP) model where motors reversibly detach into local off-track states. Using mean-field, continuum, and fast-switching approximations, we derive an effective nonlinear transport equation for total motor density. This reduced model retains the classical TASEP phase structure but reveals that increasing \(N\) shifts the boundaries between low-density, high-density, and maximal-current regimes. Crucially, under source-driven boundary conditions reflecting constant cargo production, the entrance density undergoes a saddle-node bifurcation when the production rate exceeds the network's transport capacity, \(N/4\). This triggers persistent cargo accumulation that propagates throughout the domain. Our results establish a physical mechanism by which gradual microtubule degradation drives a transition from efficient transport to jammed pathological states.
item.dc:creator: Gustav Jennetten, Bhargav R. Karamched

item.title: Widom asymptotics for spatial compressions of Schr\"odinger spectral projections
item.description: arXiv:2610.29076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a Widom trace formula for spatial compressions of exact spectral projections of semiclassical Schr\"odinger operators. The potential is smooth near a compact classically allowed region, and the observation domain lies strictly inside that region. For every continuous spectral function with positive power decay at both endpoints, we obtain a trace formula at scale $h^{1-n}\log h^{-1}$ whose coefficient separates into a boundary integral and a universal spectral functional. This yields the exact von Neumann and R\'enyi entanglement asymptotics for every fixed positive order, and proves their universal ratios to the particle-number variance. The proof combines commutator estimates in every fixed positive Schatten class with a local trace formula obtained from a boundary-adapted normal form and a Hardy model. In dimensions $n\ge2$, a positive partition and the known variance asymptotic control the grazing contribution; in one dimension all boundary Fermi points are transverse. A harmonic-oscillator counterexample shows that continuity and weighted integrability alone are insufficient for the trace formula.
item.dc:creator: Pan Ma, Daoyuan Zheng

item.title: The L\'{e}vy wave packet and fractional uncertainty relations
item.description: arXiv:2610.29397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work revisits the debate on fractional uncertainty relations that arose a decade ago and tries to settle it. After a careful study of the position-momentum uncertainty product of the L\'{e}vy wave packet, a novel lower bound is proposed for uncertainty relations in fractional quantum mechanics. This bound is nearly linear in the L\'{e}vy index and is satisfied by exact, calculable solutions available in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Zi-Xuan Li, Xiao-Dong Li, Towe Wang

item.title: Geometrization of continuum mechanics and nonequilibrium thermodynamics: Heat conduction
item.description: arXiv:2610.29644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a geometric formulation of non-equilibrium heat conduction. It combines the variational (Hamiltonian) structure of symmetric hyperbolic thermodynamically compatible (SHTC) equations with the exterior calculus of differential forms. The central object is the thermal impulse one-form on the four-dimensional matter-time manifold. Its time component is the temperature, and for reversible (ballistic) heat transport it is the exact differential of a scalar potential (i.e. it is holonomic). Non-equilibrium effects are described by a second one-form, the small-scale thermal impulse, which is not required to be exact. Its time component is a fluctuating temperature, and its exterior derivative, the four-thermal vorticity, satisfies a Bianchi-type kinematic identity. The variational principle together with this identity yields a non-equilibrium two-temperature model. Its field equations have the same structure as Maxwell's equations in a medium, with the thermal impulse field, the thermal vorticity field and a thermal Poynting vector contributing to the heat flux. Dissipation is introduced through relaxation terms that conserve the total energy and produce entropy. A formal asymptotic analysis shows that, in the relaxation limit, the model reduces to a Guyer-Krumhansl-type heat conduction with independent transverse and longitudinal length scales. The transverse nonlocal term comes from the spatial non-holonomy of the small-scale thermal impulse, while the longitudinal term comes from its non-holonomy in time, i.e. from the relaxation of the fluctuating temperature. We also discuss the gauge-theoretic interpretation of the model. Its kinematics is that of an abelian gauge theory, while the local gauge symmetry is explicitly broken by the existence of two temperatures. Finally, we discuss the consequences of the geometric structure for structure-preserving numerical methods.
item.dc:creator: Ilya Peshkov

item.title: On the planar Neumann--Poincar\'e inverse spectral problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.29661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Does the Neumann--Poincar\'e spectrum determine a planar domain up to an extended M\"obius transformation? We construct a pair showing that the answer is no, even for analytic, strictly convex, algebraic boundaries. Their operators are similar. We then prove a positive result for prescribed finite-dimensional families of normalised exterior conformal maps. For every $m\ge1$, the first $m$ positive eigenvalues determine $m$ real Laurent coefficients on a small truncated convex cone, provided the higher coefficients are a prescribed analytic remainder of quadratic order. Recovery is Lipschitz stable, uniformly down to the disk. The proof combines the Grunsky representation with a nondegeneracy argument for weighted Hankel matrices and differentiated perturbation estimates. Explicit two- and three-parameter examples, single-mode families with repeated leading eigenvalues, and M\"obius equivalence classes illustrate the result. Direct proofs for complete polarization data show what spectral weights add to the eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Habib Ammari, Matthew J. Colbrook

item.title: BCC optimality for the three-dimensional Coulomb lattice energy
item.description: arXiv:2610.29732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the body-centered cubic lattice uniquely minimizes the renormalized Coulomb energy among three-dimensional Bravais lattices of fixed covolume, up to orthogonal transformations. Using Ewald summation, we write the energy, to within an additive constant, as a sum of two positive, rapidly convergent series in real and reciprocal space. Their positivity provides finite lower bounds for all competitors. A passage to the dual lattice reduces the problem to a face-centered cubic comparison. A short basis vector estimate, a certified local Hessian, and interval bounds on a compact five-dimensional domain complete the computer-assisted proof.
item.dc:creator: C. B. Muratov, M. Novaga

item.title: Quantum Charge as a Particle/Antiparticle Label
item.description: arXiv:2610.29791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the concept of particles and antiparticles is related to the Weyl-Heisenberg group $W\!H_3$. Its generators are the position operators $\hat x^a$, the momentum operators $\hat p_a$, and the central element $Q_{\sf{v}}$, which defines a subgroup U(1)$_{\sf v}$ of $W\!H_3$. We show that the wave functions have a charge relative to the group U(1)$_{\sf{v}}$ equal to either $q_+=1/\hbar$ (particle $\psi_+$) or $q_-=-1/\hbar$ (antiparticle $\psi_-$). We call these eigenvalues of the operator $Q_{\sf{v}}$ quantum charges: $Q_{\sf{v}}\psi_\pm^{}=q_\pm^{}\psi_\pm^{}$. The wave functions $\psi_+$ and $\psi_-$ belong to the Hilbert spaces $\mathcal{H}_+$ and $\mathcal{H}_-$, on which unitarily inequivalent representations $\pi_\hbar$ and $\pi_{-\hbar}$ of the Weyl-Heisenberg group $W\!H_3$ are defined. These representations are related to each other by the antilinear charge conjugation operator $\hat C$, which maps $\mathcal{H}_+, q_+$ to $\mathcal{H}_-, q_-$. Charges $q_\pm^{}$ are intrinsic characteristics of the wave functions $\psi_\pm^{}$, similar to spin and electric charge. The wave function possesses one of these charges, $q_+$ or $q_-$, prior to the specification of any equations. We show that negative probabilities/energies and the Klein paradox in Klein-Gordon and Dirac theories are consequences of the violation of U(1)$_{\sf v}$-invariance in these theories. Restoring this invariance separates particle and antiparticles and eliminates all paradoxes at the level of first-quantized relativistic theories.
item.dc:creator: Alexander D. Popov

item.title: Generalized Coordinate Bethe Ansatz and Quantum Integrability of the Time-Dependent Massive Thirring Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.29998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a generalized coordinate Bethe-ansatz framework for the massive Thirring model with an explicitly time-dependent fermion mass. Unlike the generalized Bethe ansatz for chiral quantum field theories, where particle transport acts in internal spin spaces and leads to quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations, the present construction acts directly on particle coordinates and physical rapidities. Its central new feature is a rapidity lattice. Because the time-dependent mass couples right- and left-moving components already in the one-particle sector, a fixed-rapidity block is not closed under spatial winding. Periodicity therefore requires all sectors generated by the finite shift $\beta\to\beta-p$. Particle exchange relates amplitudes on this lattice through scalar analytic difference equations of Ruijsenaars type, whose solutions determine the complete time-dependent many-body wavefunction. Consistency of the coordinate construction also selects an exponential evolution of the bare mass, providing a new realization of the time dependent integrability-renormalization group correspondence. In the static limit, the rapidity-lattice construction reduces to the conventional massive-Thirring Bethe equations. Through the massive-Thirring/sine Gordon equivalence, the result also connects this exact quantum construction to the generalized space-time dependent Lax formalism.
item.dc:creator: Parameshwar R. Pasnoori

item.title: Mellin transformed exponential volumes and probabilistic moduli spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.26580v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A decorated surface is a surface with boundary and a finite set of marked boundary points called cusps. We continue to study the exponential volumes E(S,K,L) of moduli spaces of ideal hyperbolic structures on a decorated surface S, with the given values of lengths of boundary geodesic circles L and boundary geodesic intervals K, introduced in our previous work: 1. We prove that the Mellin--Laplace transform of E(S,K,L) admits Barnes integral presentations, and satisfies recursions, generalising Mirzakhani's recursions. 2. We specify a subset I of the blue boundary intervals, and assign to them any collection of weights. We show that the Mellin transform of the function E(S,K,L) along the variables K at the blue intervals, evaluated at the weights values, calculates weighted exponential volumes of various moduli spaces. If all boundary intervals are blue and all weights are 1/2, we recover Chekhov's volumes of moduli spaces of hyperbolic surfaces with crowns, discretizing the Schwarzian action. We derive recursions for the weighted exponential volumes. 3. We introduce probabilistic Teichmuller spaces related to decorated surfaces S. They are infinite dimensional and carry canonical Wiener type measures. The definition of the measures builds on the works of Bauerschmidt - Losev - Wildemann and Losev. Their quotients by the action of the modular group of S are probabilistic moduli spaces. We show that their volumes are finite. We prove recursion formulas for these measures, and hence for the volumes. The emerging theory generalizes the Schwarzian field theory of Stanford - Witten from the disc to any decorated surfaces, i.e. to open string format. In particular, we get recursions for the Feynman integrals in Schwarzian field theory on decorated surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Alexander B. Goncharov, Zhe Sun

item.title: Percolation on Bidirected Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.28762v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study bidirected percolation on an undirected graph $G$: each edge is replaced by two oppositely directed edges, each of which is open independently with probability $p$. Two vertices are strongly connected if they are mutually reachable by open directed paths. Let $p_\mathrm{sc}$ denote the threshold for the existence of an infinite strongly connected cluster, and let $p_c$ denote the usual Bernoulli percolation threshold on $G$. On every transitive amenable graph, we prove that $p_\mathrm{sc}=p_c$. In contrast, sufficiently spread-out modifications of every transitive non-amenable graph satisfy $p_\mathrm{sc}>p_c$. We also show that, on $\mathbb Z^d$ with $d\ge11$, the expected size of the strongly connected cluster is finite at $p=p_\mathrm{sc}$.
item.dc:creator: Yucheng Liu, Leonardo T. Rolla, Yuliang Shi

item.title: The Prevalence of Straight Shots in Control Space for Reaching Optimal Quantum Performance
item.description: arXiv:2610.28852v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gradient-based algorithms are often applied to identify an optimal control for maximizing a quantum objective functional by following a steepest ascent path to the top of the control landscape. In contrast, this paper explores straight shots through control space where movement along such a path corresponds to a less demanding monotonic complete climb up the landscape for the optimal objective value. Existing studies of control landscapes have revealed the presence of straight shots, but identifying them required computationally intensive stochastic methods. In this paper, we introduce a non-stochastic straight-shot search algorithm (STSA) that identifies a large class of straight shots. We apply STSA to numerically generate more than 10,000 distinct straight-shot optimization paths and analyze their statistical distribution for each of the objectives of (i) state-to-state transitions, (ii) general observables, and (iii) unitary transformation generation. The results show a decrease in the nearest-neighbor distances among straight shots as the sample size increases, suggesting their prevalence in control space. We further conjecture that the starting locations of the straight-shot pathways on a landscape level set may form connected neighborhoods, motivating future investigation into their underlying topological structure. The present paper focuses on the use of STSA for locating massive numbers of straight solutions. However, the STSA is not a high-efficiency algorithm in its present form, but the discovered prevalence of control straight shots leaves open future advances to accelerate the discovery of straight shots as optimal controls.
item.dc:creator: Yiyou Chen, Gabriele Herr, Herschel Rabitz

item.title: "Massive" Conformal Field Theories and application to Nambu-Goto string
item.description: arXiv:2610.28888v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: I describe the recent progress in understanding diffeomorphism invariant two-dimensional theories with dimensionful parameters which have nevertheless traceless improved energy-momentum tensor and turn out to be conformal invariant. An example is the Liouville theory with the additional four-derivative terms arising from the Nambu-Goto string and telling apart the Nambu-Goto and Polyakov strings. Its exact solution in embedding dimension d=4 is consistent in contrast to the Polyakov string and described by the (4,3) unitary minimal model. Talk at Irina Aref'eva Conference "Perspective Directions in Quantum Field Theory and Superstrings", Moscow 12-17 October 2026.
item.dc:creator: Yuri Makeenko

item.title: The Octonionic Rational Wave Numbers: Non-Associative Sequence Algebras, Moufang Loops, and Exceptional $G_2$ Symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2610.28921v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We generalize discrete rational wave numbers (arXiv:2609.23233) to the octonionic rational wave numbers $\mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ over Cayley's octonions $\mathbb{O}$. Rather than assuming higher imaginary units, all rational wave number spaces $\mathbb{C}^\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{H}^\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ are derived constructively from two scalar primitives: the coordinate advance $E_Z$ and phase calibration $E_{\bar{1}}$. Their closure under pointwise multiplication, inversion, and rational roots generates an infinite divisible Moufang loop on the sequence ring $\mathcal{S}_\mathbb{O} := \mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$, terminating strictly at $\mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ via sedenionic zero-divisor excision. By Artin's Theorem, pairwise compositions remain strictly associative, whereas three-wave interactions generate an intrinsic non-associative curvature quantified by the associator $[u, v, w] = (uv)w - u(vw)$. We define a real-valued sequence inner product that bypasses the Jordan--von Neumann--Wigner obstruction, establishing the orthonormality of the seven Fano coordinate primitives. We establish three principal theorems: (1) The Invariant Hexagonal Mesh Theorem, proving that cumulative integration exhibits a scale-invariant bifurcation at $n=6$ governed by the root system of $G_2 = \operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb{O})$ and its $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ stabilizer subgroup; (2) The Algebraic Phase Jitter Theorem, showing that Catalan parenthesization trees across non-Fano triads produce an irreducible zero-point phase fluctuation, yielding an algebraic origin for vacuum jitter; and (3) The Rational Loop Closure Theorem, proving that rational frequencies select closed finite Moufang sub-loops, while irrational frequencies yield topologically dense, non-closing trajectories. This provides an autonomous, discrete algebraic foundation for non-associative geometry and fundamental physical symmetries.
item.dc:creator: Terence R. Smith

item.title: Sharp Quantitative Convergence of Compactly Supported Aggregation-Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.29000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish the quantitative convergence of nonlinear aggregation-diffusion equations in dimension one, with sublinear attraction kernel and degenerate diffusion higher than quadratic. In these models, steady state is known to be the unique, compactly supported, and radial decreasing probability distribution. In this paper, we work with compactly supported densities in dimension one, we prove these solutions converge to the steady state exponentially fast.
item.dc:creator: Yunhong Deng

item.title: Adapted Fr\"ohlich-Pizzo Model for Horizon-Induced Decoherence
item.description: arXiv:2610.29363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Fr\"ohlich-Pizzo (FP) model is a quantum-mechanical model originally developed to describe the interaction between an atom and the electromagnetic field in the nonrelativistic limit $c\to\infty$. We show that an adaptation of the FP model based on the local algebras of a $U(1)$ chiral current captures essential features of the horizon-induced decoherence mechanism identified by Danielson, Satishchandran, and Wald (DSW) in the limit of large holding time $T$. Our analysis suggests that the effective dynamics of the system undergoing decoherence in the DSW setting retains non-Markovian features. Our approach also offers a glimpse into the possible role of quantum events in the dynamics underlying horizon-induced decoherence.
item.dc:creator: Bik-Soon Sia

item.title: A spinor-adapted geometric approach to nonlinear Dirac systems on the Schwarzschild black hole background
item.description: arXiv:2610.29406v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Building on our previous work, we extend the spinor-adapted geometric method for nonlinear Dirac systems from small perturbations of Minkowski spacetime to the Schwarzschild background. As a linear foundation, we establish integrated local energy decay estimates and an \(r^p\)-weighted energy hierarchy for spinor fields, adapting the physical-space approach of Dafermos and Rodnianski to the Dirac setting. The main focus of the paper is nonlinear. We consider a semilinear tensorial wave--Dirac model motivated by the wave-gauge reduction of the Einstein--Dirac system and prove global small-data stability. A principal difficulty is the apparent loss of derivatives arising from the coupling between the first-order Dirac equation and the second-order tensorial wave equation. We overcome this difficulty through a spinor-adapted energy hierarchy that exploits the complementary roles of the Dirac-current energy and the spinorial wave energy. In particular, the nonlinear estimates are closed without requiring the top-order Dirac-current estimate. The nonlinear analysis demonstrates that the spinorial structures remain essential on the black-hole background. The combination of Dirac-current energy, spinorial wave energy, Kosmann Lie derivatives, and the Clifford-algebraic null structure enables us to close the nonlinear estimates without imposing an independent null condition on the tensorial wave equation. Thus, the nonlinear closure relies fundamentally on structures intrinsic to the Dirac equation. A second main result is the global small-data stability of the Maxwell--Dirac system in the Lorenz gauge on the Schwarzschild background, under a vanishing-charge assumption. This extends the nonlinear stability theory to a genuine gauge-coupled Dirac system and demonstrates the applicability of the spinor-adapted physical-space approach beyond the tensorial wave--Dirac model.
item.dc:creator: Seokchang Hong

item.title: Maximal velocity estimates for Hardy operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.29513v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove maximal velocity estimates for the fractional Laplacian with an added subcritical Hardy potential, called Hardy operator, and possibly external potentials. As an application, we give another proof of the nonexistence of the wave operator intertwining Hardy operators with and without long-range perturbations with Coulomb decay.
item.dc:creator: Atsuhide Ishida, Konstantin Merz

item.title: Stochastic resonance in time-delayed bistable active particles
item.description: arXiv:2610.29601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate analytically and numerically stochastic resonance in an underdamped active (Ornstein--Uhlenbeck) particle confined in a bistable potential with time-delayed feedback and subjected to an additional (non-thermal) white-noise source. Restricting the analysis to the active-noise-dominated bistable regime, with sufficiently short delay and active-noise correlation times, we develop a perturbative theory that yields analytical expressions for both the escape rate and the spectral power amplification within the framework of linear-response theory, without invoking detailed balance. The analytical predictions are in qualitative agreement with direct numerical simulations throughout the perturbative regime. We show that a moderate increase in the active-noise correlation time can enhance the stochastic-resonance response, in marked contrast to previous results for overdamped passive systems driven by colored noise. Conversely, the addition of white noise weakens the resonant response and shifts its optimum toward lower active-noise intensities. Time-delayed feedback further alters the matching condition between the escape rate and the driving frequency while preserving the resonant mechanism. Beyond the perturbative regime, we find that finite-memory effects progressively broaden the resonance profile and substantially decrease its amplitude. Overall, these results provide new insight into the combined role of inertia, activity, environmental fluctuations, and time delayed feedback in stochastic resonance in nonequilibrium systems.
item.dc:creator: Antonio A. Valido, Mattia Coccolo, Miguel A. F. Sanju\'an

item.title: Fermion-Number Variation for Several Coupling Schemes in an $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Chiral Soliton Background
item.description: arXiv:2610.29632v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When topological solitons are coupled to fermions, they often induce a nontrivial fermion number. In the chiral quark soliton model (CQSM), this phenomenon underlies the identification of soliton topology with baryon number. However, whether this topology--fermion-number correspondence is determined solely by soliton topology or also depends on the fermion--soliton coupling scheme remains unclear. In this paper, we investigate this question by comparing several coupling schemes to the same $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ chiral soliton background. To treat the corresponding Dirac Hamiltonians within a common framework, we evaluate the variation of the regularized fermion-number along a model-parameter space. For the standard chiral Yukawa coupling of the CQSM, this variation reproduces the topological charge $Q$ associated with $\pi_3(\mathrm{SU}(N))$. The same result is obtained for an axial-vector coupling, whereas the fermion number variation vanishes for a vector coupling, despite the nontrivial topology of the chiral soliton background. These results provide an explicit example in which soliton topology alone does not determine the fermionic response; the topology--fermion-number correspondence also depends on how the background field is coupled to fermions.
item.dc:creator: Nobuyuki Sawado, Shintaro Yamamoto

item.title: Quantum f-divergences from retrodiction: a unifying classical variational principle
item.description: arXiv:2610.29696v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The same classical f-divergence admits inequivalent extensions to quantum states. The question is whether these extensions can be obtained from a common operational variational principle. Here we generalize Matsumoto's reverse-test optimization by introducing a reference prior state. More explicitly, we minimize the statistical distinguishability between a forward and a reverse prepare-and-measure process, related by retrodiction through the chosen reference and subject to prescribed quantum averages. Distinguishability is quantified by the classical f-divergence between their complete records. For faithful states in finite dimension, we prove that the same spectral implementation attains the minimum simultaneously for every operator-convex f. Varying the reference allows us to interpolate between standard and maximal quantum f-divergences of the prescribed states, passing through the geodesic family. More precisely, a flat reference yields the standard quantum f-divergences, thereby giving the Nussbaum-Szko{\l}a distributions a variational characterization as optimal records. Choosing either prescribed state as reference recovers maximal quantum f-divergences and Matsumoto's reverse tests, while power references realize the geodesic interpolation. In the relative-entropy case, this gives the passage from Umegaki to Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy by changing the prior for retrodiction.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Buscemi

item.title: The sharp Chern--Simons--Sobolev inequality and its variants
item.description: arXiv:2610.29769v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce and prove a new conformally invariant Chern--Simons--Sobolev inequality, and classify all optimizers, which are the Hopf map $\pi:\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}\to\mathbb{CP}^n$ composed with a symplectic diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and an orientation-preserving conformal transformation of $\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}$. The proof uses the sharp curl-Sobolev inequality and a rigidity argument for its equality case. Motivated by the main result, we also introduce the spherical Radu--Tchrakian--Yang functional, and prove the global minimality of the Hopf map for radii in a neighborhood of $((n!)^2/n)^{1/(4n-4)}$, and characterize all minimizers. We also prove local instability for sufficiently small and sufficiently large radii, with explicit lower bounds for the Morse index.
item.dc:creator: Mingwei Zhang

item.title: On unitary vertex operator algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.29878v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a conformal vertex algebra with a non-zero invariant Hermitian form is unitary as soon as it admits a non-zero positive energy module with a positive definite invariant Hermitian form. Using free field realizations, we deduce that the principal simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g)$ of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ is unitary for central charge $c\ge rank(\mathfrak g)+24\bigl((\rho|\rho^\vee)+\|\rho\|\,\|\rho^\vee\|\bigr)$, and, if $\mathfrak g$ is simply laced, for all $c\ge rank(\mathfrak g)$. Among basic Lie superalgebras which are not Lie algebras, the free field argument applies to $osp(1|2n)$ and $osp(2|2n)$. It shows that $W_k(osp(1|2n))$ is unitary for $c\ge n+\frac12$ and gives an explicit bound for $osp(2|2n)$. Next, we prove that if $\mathfrak s$ is an even $sl_2$-subalgebra of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ whose centralizer is not abelian, then the simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak s)$ is unitary for at most finitely many $k$. We illustrate this on the $W$-algebras of $sl_{qm}$ attached to the nilpotents of Jordan type $q^m$: unitarity is possible only at two levels, and for $q=2$ it does occur at both. For instance, the $W$-algebra of $sl_4$ attached to the partition $2+2$ is unitary only for $k=-2$ and $k=-\frac32$. This fails for Lie superalgebras, as minimal $W$-algebras show, but still holds under stronger assumptions. Finally, we prove that a simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak s)$ can be unitary for only finitely many $k$ if $\mathfrak g$ is a simple Lie algebra and $\mathfrak s$ is not a distinguished $sl_2$ subalgebra.
item.dc:creator: Victor G. Kac, Pierluigi M\"oseneder Frajria, Paolo Papi

item.title: Painlev\'e representations for joint moments of characteristic polynomials from the orthogonal and unitary symplectic groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.29947v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study joint moments of characteristic polynomials and their second derivatives for Haar-distributed matrices from the unitary symplectic and orthogonal groups. We establish their large-$N$ asymptotics throughout the full admissible range of the moment parameters and identify the limiting coefficients probabilistically in terms of the first inverse power sum of the Bessel point process. This extends the corresponding results of Assiotis, Gunes, Keating, and Wei [Proc. Lond. Math. Soc., 132 (2026), e70136] to the full admissible parameter range. Throughout this full range, we also express these limits in terms of a distinguished solution of the $\sigma$-Painlev\'e III' equation. Our approach reduces the problem to singular inverse-power statistics of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and combines their finite-$N$ $\sigma$-Painlev\'e V representation with a refined Riemann-Hilbert analysis yielding precise small-$x$ asymptotics and uniform derivative estimates for the finite-$N$ correction term. A key ingredient in the probabilistic identification is a kernel-based proof that the rescaled first inverse power sum of the Jacobi ensemble converges in distribution to its Bessel point process counterpart.
item.dc:creator: Theodoros Assiotis, Thomas Bothner, Jonathan P. Keating, Nicholas Simm, Fei Wei

item.title: Finite Classification of Transversal Diagonal Gates Beyond Stabilizer Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.29955v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish that transversal diagonal gates on exact qubit codes of distance at least two can be exhaustively classified within a finite search space. Although code-preserving physical gates can have continuous phases, any projective logical action induced by a transversal diagonal gate can always be realized by a physical gate of finite order. Crucially, we prove that this physical order has an upper bound determined solely by the code parameters. This order bound enables the subset-sum-linear-programming (SSLP) framework introduced in arXiv:2504.20847 to exhaustively enumerate all candidate discrete symmetries, after which the Knill-Laflamme equations determine the remaining continuous code parameters. Applying this method to the nontrivial diagonal sector of exact $((6,2,3))$ codes, SSLP yields $66$ candidate symmetry classes, of which exactly $15$ are realizable, supporting full projective diagonal logical cyclic groups of orders $2$, $3$, and $5$. In particular, for order $5$, the code is unique up to local unitaries and qubit permutations, equivalent to the code constructed in arXiv:2504.20847. This code also attains the minimum length $n=6$ among exact $((n, 2, \ge 3))$ codes whose full projective transversal group cannot be conjugated into the projective Clifford group.
item.dc:creator: Xi He, Chao Zhang, Shilin Huang, Bei Zeng

item.title: Relative geometry of nuclear mean fields through differential forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.30046v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Proton and neutron densities can have similar multipole moments while differing locally. We use differential forms to measure and locate such differences between nuclear mean fields. A pair invariant measures the angle between two density gradients, weighted by their magnitudes, and the coarea formula resolves its contribution over level surfaces. A triple invariant factorizes exactly into a weighted pair term and a directional term that measures the variation of a third field along the level-surface intersections. We test these quantities in 98 magnetized Wigner-Seitz solutions, five static Hartree-Fock configurations, an illustrative $^{16}$O + $^{34}$Mg collision, and periodic nuclear pasta (a slab and a connected network). The pair invariant distinguishes cell solutions with comparable proton quadrupole moments and is 253 times larger in $^{34}$Mg than in $^{24}$Mg; refinement to 0.6 fm changes it by at most 1.3% in the four configurations recomputed. The directional factor separates the sampled triaxial configurations from the prolate ones. In the collision, it accounts for the 7.3-fold rise of the triple before the first recorded low-density connection, while the weighted pair term changes by at most 3%. In nuclear pasta, slab and network configurations have similar integrated proton-neutron misalignment but different distributions over density levels; their triple invariants differ by a factor of about 370 on the finer grid, mainly due to the variation of the Coulomb potential along joint density levels. These comparisons require no preferred origin or axis. A resolved nonzero triple excludes a common symmetry axis, but zero does not establish one. The pasta results require further convergence studies.
item.dc:creator: Rafael C. R. de Lima

item.title: AnyonWiki.org
item.description: arXiv:2610.30081v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The AnyonWiki is an open-source project that provides full algebraic and numerical data of fusion and unitary modular fusion categories as a resource for the scientific community. It comes with a database, the AnyonWikiDatabase, that currently includes the classification of multiplicity-free pivotal (braided) fusion categories through rank 7 and more than 25000 fusion rings including the classification of multiplicity-free fusion rings through rank 10, with work in progress to expand. This data is available through AnyonWiki.org, a website that provides robust search and download functionality and presents each fusion ring and category via a dedicated webpage. In this short article we discuss the data available at AnyonWiki.org as well as the scientific and communal motivations for the design of its underlying AnyonWikiDatabase, which are centered around making the data accessible, independently verifiable, granularly citable, useful, and easy to work with.
item.dc:creator: Colleen Delaney, Ralph Razzouk, Joost Slingerland, Gert Vercleyen

item.title: Scaling H2 Factorization to Billion-Unknown Three-Dimensional Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.30131v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Strong recursive skeletonization provides approximate direct solvers for dense matrices from integral equations and kernel methods, but distributed implementations face substantial communication costs and limited parallelism, especially in three dimensions. We present a distributed-memory $\mathcal{H}^2$ factorization solver for symmetric matrices that combines spatial box coloring, delayed Schur complement updates, streamed sketching-based interpolative decomposition, and BLAS-3 and shared-memory kernels. Spatial coloring enables every process to participate in each boundary stage, while delayed updates and streamed sketching reduce dense storage and communication. To our knowledge, this is the first distributed-memory strong recursive skeletonization factorization demonstrated for three-dimensional volume integral equations at billion-unknown scale. Experiments on up to 512 compute nodes demonstrate factorization of a three-dimensional Laplace system with 3.62 billion unknowns, alongside three-dimensional Helmholtz tests and a two-dimensional Mat\'ern system with 268 million unknowns. Combining streamed sketching and fully delayed updates reduces factorization time by $6.9\times$ for Laplace and $8.5\times$ for Helmholtz relative to the unsketched, eager configuration, while reducing maximum per-process resident memory by 57\% and 54\%, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Tianyu Liang, Chao Chen, James Demmel, Yang Liu

item.title: A Tight-binding Approach for Computing Subwavelength Guided Modes in Crystals with Line Defects
item.description: arXiv:2512.05370v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we develop a framework for computing subwavelength guided modes in high-contrast periodic media with line defects, based on a tight-binding approximation. The physical problem is formulated as an eigenvalue problem for the Helmholtz equation with high-contrast parameters. By employing layer potential theory on unbounded domains, we characterize the subwavelength frequencies via the quasi-periodic capacitance matrix. Our main contribution is the proof of exponential decay of the off-diagonal elements of the associated full and quasi-periodic capacitance matrices. These decay properties provide error bounds for the banded approximation of the capacitance matrices, thereby enabling a tight-binding approach for computing the spectral properties of subwavelength resonators with non-compact defects. Numerical experiments illustrate the decay and compare full and banded capacitance matrices for defect and dimerized interface configurations.
item.dc:creator: Habib Ammari, Erik Orvehed Hiltunen, Ping Liu, Borui Miao, Yi Zhu

item.title: From BV-BFV Quantization to Reshetikhin-Turaev Invariants
item.description: arXiv:2604.04556v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a program for bridging the gap between the perturbative BV-BFV quantization of Chern-Simons theory and the non-perturbative Reshetikhin-Turaev (RT) invariants of 3-manifolds, passing through factorization homology of $\mathbb{E}_n$-algebras and the derived algebraic geometry of character stacks. We conjecture that the modular tensor category underlying the RT construction arises as the $\mathbb{E}_2$-category from BV-BFV quantization of Chern-Simons theory on the disk, with the derived character stack $\mathrm{Loc}_{G_\mathbb{C}}(\Sigma)$ of the complexified group and its shifted symplectic structure mediating the proposed identification. A recurring theme is the mismatch between the compact gauge group of Chern-Simons theory and the reductive algebraic group of derived algebraic geometry: we work throughout with $G_\mathbb{C}$ and indicate where a Riemann-Hilbert type comparison is needed to return to the compact theory. We formulate a main conjecture asserting natural equivalence of the BV-BFV and RT constructions as 3-2-1-extended topological quantum field theories, together with several auxiliary conjectures and two questions, develop a proof strategy via deformation quantization of shifted symplectic stacks, and clarify the role of $\mathbb{E}_n$-Koszul duality, which relates the perturbative expansion around a flat connection to the local geometry of the character stack. We relate the perturbative expansions to the sheaf of vanishing cycles on the character stack of a $3$-manifold, propose that a stratification of the character stack by stabilizer type organizes the trans-series decomposition, and propose that the Stokes data of the perturbative expansion should be read as a stability datum in the sense of Kontsevich-Soibelman, with the Chern-Simons functional playing the role of the central charge.
item.dc:creator: Nima Moshayedi

item.title: The Fock Space Dynamics of Causal Fermion Systems: Non-Abelian Gauge Fields
item.description: arXiv:2607.08488v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A limiting case is worked out in which the causal action principle for causal fermion systems describing Minkowski space gives rise to the linear Fock space dynamics of perturbative quantum field theory, including non-abelian gauge fields and Dirac fields.
item.dc:creator: Claudio Dappiaggi, Felix Finster, Niky Kamran, Moritz Reintjes

item.title: Congruence of Dirac operators with applications to generalized MIT bag models
item.description: arXiv:2607.26675v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We highlight a simple congruence transform that shifts coupling parameters for Dirac operators with shell interactions. As one of the consequences, this leads to new observations concerning the self-adjointness and the infinite mass interpretation of generalized MIT bag models.
item.dc:creator: Joaquim Duran, Konstantin Pankrashkin

item.title: Non-Geometric T-Duality as Higher Groupoid Bundles with Connections
item.description: arXiv:2204.01783v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a description of T-duality between general geometric and non-geometric backgrounds as higher groupoid bundles with connections. Our description extends the previous observation by Nikolaus and Waldorf that the topological aspects of geometric and half-geometric T-dualities can be described in terms of higher geometry. We extend their construction in two ways. First, we endow the higher geometries with adjusted connections, which allow us to discuss explicit formulas for the metric and the Kalb-Ramond field of a T-background. Second, we extend the principal 2-bundles to principal 2-groupoid bundles, which accommodate the scalar fields arising in T-dualities along two directions as well as $Q$-fluxes. Our proposals reproduce key examples from the literature. They are manifestly covariant under the full T-duality group $\mathsf{GO}(n,n;\mathbb{Z})$ and have interesting physical and mathematical implications. Eventually, we also comment on the case of T-duality in the presence of scalar fluxes.
item.dc:creator: Hyungrok Kim, Christian Saemann

item.title: Port-Hamiltonian systems with energy and power ports
item.description: arXiv:2405.01241v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend the port-Hamiltonian framework defined with respect to a Lagrangian submanifold and a Dirac structure by augmenting the Lagrangian submanifold with the space of external variables. The new pair of conjugated variables is called energy port. We show that in the most general case, the extension describes constrained Hamiltonian systems whose Hamiltonian function depends on inputs.
item.dc:creator: Kaja Krhac, Bernhard Maschke, Arjan van der Schaft

item.title: Normal forms of elliptic automorphic Lie algebras and Landau-Lifshitz type of equations
item.description: arXiv:2412.20482v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present normal forms of elliptic automorphic Lie algebras with dihedral symmetry of order 4, which arise naturally in the context of Landau-Lifshitz type of equations. These normal forms provide a transparent description and allow a classification of such Lie algebras over $\mathbb{C}$. Using this perspective, we show that a Lie algebra introduced by Uglov, as well as the hidden symmetry algebra of the Landau-Lifshitz equation introduced by Holod, can each be realised as an elliptic $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})$-current algebra. Furthermore, we realise the Wahlquist-Estabrook algebra of the Landau-Lifshitz equation in terms of elliptic automorphic Lie algebras. This construction reveals that, as a complex Lie algebra, it is isomorphic to the direct sum of an $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})$-current algebra and the two-dimensional abelian Lie algebra $\mathbb{C}^2$. Finally, we apply the automorphic Lie algebra framework to an $n$-component generalisation of the Landau-Lifshitz equation due to Golubchik and Sokolov in the case $n=3$.
item.dc:creator: Sara Lombardo, Casper Oelen

item.title: Existence and Smoothing for a Nondivergence-Form Degenerate Diffusion from Plasma-Wave Theory
item.description: arXiv:2503.13922v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove existence and positive-time smoothing of weak solutions to the degenerate parabolic Cauchy--Dirichlet problem $\partial_t u = \rho_\lambda(x)u\,\partial_x^2 u + \rho_\lambda(x)g(x)u$ on the half-line, where $\rho_\lambda$ vanishes at the boundary and grows at infinity. This scalar problem arises from a formal reduction of the one-dimensional quasilinear system for plasma waves, which couples an electron distribution to a wave-energy spectrum: we develop a solution theory for the scalar problem that lifts to this system. For the scalar problem, we construct nonnegative weak solutions under weighted integrability assumptions on the initial data and boundedness of the reaction coefficient $\rho_\lambda g$, admitting unbounded and discontinuous data pertinent to the physical model. We establish a one-sided bound on $\partial_t u$ which yields positive-time smoothing: solutions become locally H\"older continuous in both space and time and locally Lipschitz continuous in space. Explicit examples show that this spatial regularity is sharp. Under natural assumptions on the initial data, our scalar solutions lift to weak solutions of the particle--wave system that preserve nonnegativity, conserve particle mass, smooth initial particle measures to locally bounded densities at positive times, and exhibit quantitative decay of the wave spectrum at large wavenumber.
item.dc:creator: William Porteous, Irene M. Gamba, Kun Huang

item.title: On electrostatic manifolds with boundary
item.description: arXiv:2505.05581v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Static manifolds with boundary were recently introduced in the context of the problem of prescribing both the scalar curvature of a Riemannian manifold and the mean curvature of its boundary. These manifolds are also of interest from the perspective of general relativity. In this article, we introduce electrostatic manifolds with boundary as a natural generalization of static manifolds with boundary in the presence of a nonzero electric field. We also introduce Robin electrostatic quadruples, extending the notion of Robin static triples previously introduced by the second author. We establish several uniqueness theorems for suitable regions of the Reissner-Nordstr\"om manifold. Finally, we characterize the criticality of the first eigenvalue of an associated mixed Robin-Dirichlet Schr\"odinger operator under admissible volume-preserving variations in terms of the equality of the surface gravities along the Dirichlet boundary components.
item.dc:creator: Stanislav Demurov, Vladimir Medvedev

item.title: Noncommutative principal bundles and central extensions
item.description: arXiv:2509.02263v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by the classical theory of spin structures, we develop a theory for lifting free C$^*$-dynamical systems, a.k.a. noncommutative principal bundles, along central extensions. This theory extends the bundle-theoretic notion of spin structures and yields a complete existence and classification result for such lifts. Using factor system techniques and Picard formalism, our approach introduces new invariants and obstruction classes, thereby unifying geometric, cohomological, and operator-algebraic perspectives. A range of examples demonstrates the scope of the theory.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Wagner

item.title: Hyperbolic $O (N)$ linear sigma model and its mean-field limit
item.description: arXiv:2511.21950v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study large $N$ limits of the hyperbolic $O(N)$ linear sigma model ($\text{HLSM}_N$) on the two-dimensional torus $\mathbb T^2$, namely, a system of $N$ interacting stochastic damped nonlinear wave equations (SdNLW) with coupled cubic nonlinearities. After establishing (pathwise) global well-posedness of $\text{HLSM}_N$ and the limiting equation, called the mean-field SdNLW, we first establish global-in-time convergence of $\text{HLSM}_N$ to the mean-field SdNLW with general initial data (under a suitable assumption). In particular, for the local-in-time convergence, we obtain a convergence rate of order $N^{- \frac 12}$ under an additional integrability assumption on initial data. We then show that the invariant Gibbs dynamics for $\text{HLSM}_N$ converges to that for the mean-field SdNLW with a convergence rate of order $N^{- \frac 12}$ on any large time intervals.
item.dc:creator: Ruoyuan Liu, Shao Liu, Tadahiro Oh

item.title: Edge universality in Floquet sideband spectra
item.description: arXiv:2604.05244v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A monochromatic voltage drive redistributes noninteracting fermions over sidebands with Bessel amplitudes. A sharp Fermi step gives the discrete Bessel source kernel, whose large amplitude edge has the Airy limit known from random matrices and propagating fronts. At zero temperature and for energy independent transmission, the deficit of the dc bias derivative of low frequency partition noise from its large bias slope is proportional to the kernel diagonal, with ac amplitude fixed. Shifting the integer threshold coordinate down by half a sideband removes the leading finite amplitude correction. For reservoirs at a common temperature, we derive the rescaled deficit's crossover through one thermal convolution per reservoir. Its leading low temperature correction is twice that of the rescaled source occupation. We specify the geometry and mode resolution needed to distinguish this signature from the full Airy point process.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Tierz

item.title: Depth dependence of entanglement and circuit complexity in random linear optical networks
item.description: arXiv:2604.14277v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the growth of entanglement and circuit complexity in random passive linear optical networks as a function of the circuit depth. For entanglement dynamics, we start with an initial Gaussian state with all $n$ modes equally squeezed. For random brickwork circuits, we show that entanglement, as measured by the R\'enyi-2 entropy, grows diffusively as a function of the depth, in contrast to the linear growth for random qubit brickwork circuits. In the other direction, for arbitrary circuit geometries we prove bounds on depths which ensure the average-case subsystem entanglement reaches within a constant factor of the maximum value in all subsystems, and bounds which ensure closeness of the random linear optical unitary to a Haar random unitary in $L^2$ Wasserstein distance. We also consider robust circuit complexity for random one-dimensional brickwall circuits, as measured by the minimum number of gates required in any circuit that approximately implements the linear optical unitary. Viewing this as a function of the number of modes and the circuit depth, we show the robust circuit complexity for random one-dimensional brickwall circuits scales at most diffusively in the depth with high probability, again in contrast to the linear scaling for certain random qubit circuits. The corresponding Gaussian unitary $\tilde{\mathcal U}$ for the approximate implementation retains high output fidelity $|\langle\psi|\mathcal U^\dagger \tilde{\mathcal U}|\psi\rangle|^2$ for pure states $|\psi\rangle$ with constrained expected photon-number.
item.dc:creator: Laura Shou, Joseph T. Iosue, Yu-Xin Wang, Victor Galitski, Alexey V. Gorshkov

item.title: Batalin-Vilkovisky quantization with an angular twist
item.description: arXiv:2604.16225v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct cubic scalar field theory on $\lambda$-Minkowski space by combining the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism with harmonic analysis, and produce two inequivalent noncommutative quantum field theories. The braided theory is based on a braided $L_\infty$-algebra whereby covariance dictates a spectral decomposition into cylindrical Bessel functions that diagonalise the angular Drinfel'd twist; in this theory we find the usual logarithmic ultraviolet divergences and confirm the absence of UV/IR mixing. The standard noncommutative theory is based on a classical $L_\infty$-algebra; in this theory we relate the spectral decompositions into plane wave and cylindrical harmonic eigenmodes of the Klein-Gordan operator, we verify the planar equivalence theorem, and we demonstrate a periodic form of UV/IR mixing in which non-planar correlators are generically ultraviolet finite but become non-analytic on an infinite lattice of exceptional momenta.
item.dc:creator: Djordje Bogdanovi\'c, Marija Dimitrijevi\'c \'Ciri\'c, Richard J. Szabo

item.title: Non-symmetric vector dyson equations
item.description: arXiv:2607.16333v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the vector Dyson equation $$-\frac{1}{m(z)}=z\mathbf{1}-\mathbf{a}+Sm(z),$$ with parameter $z$ in the complex upper half-plane $\mathbb{C}_+$, where $\mathbf{a}\in\mathbb R^d$ and $S$ is a nonnegative matrix, not necessarily symmetric. This equation has a unique vector solution $m(z)\in\mathbb{C}_+^d$, for which we establish a complete measure decomposition and prove regularity. We then develop a graph-theoretic approach to the singularity and stability problem for non-symmetric matrices $S$. The graph structure of $S$ identifies the possible degeneracies of the stability operator as $z$ approaches the real axis. In particular, for non-backtracking matrices, we prove square-root growth at regular edges, cubic-root growth at regular cusps, and complete stability estimates. We also obtain the corresponding estimates for symmetric matrices in the periodic setting.
item.dc:creator: Jiaoyang Huang, Zhonggen Su, Ruizhe Xu

item.title: Exact quantum circuits for a lattice Boltzmann realization of the Dirac equation
item.description: arXiv:2608.06570v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The quantum lattice Boltzmann scheme of Succi and Dellar advances a four-component Dirac spinor on a lattice by a fixed sequence of local, exactly norm-preserving operations: a basis rotation, a collision, a streaming shift, and the inverse rotation. While this correspondence has been noted qualitatively, it has remained unclear whether it can be realized exactly and unitarily as a gate-model quantum circuit. This unitarity is a structural property of the scheme, which should, in principle, enable an operator-by-operator port onto quantum hardware. We give a gate-level construction of every operation of the three-dimensional Dirac QLB scheme: the fixed rotation gates, the collision gate, the streaming shift as a controlled increment on a position register, the position-dependent potential as a phase oracle, and periodic and reflecting boundary conditions as unitary circuits. Together, these constructions provide the first complete demonstration that the scheme is exactly representable in the gate model without any approximation beyond the classical method itself. We then compose them into single-axis, two- and three-dimensional time steps. On a state-vector emulator the resulting circuits reproduce the classical QLB solver to machine precision, thus verifying our quantum implementation. Our aim is representability and correctness rather than computational speedup; questions of state preparation, asymptotic cost, and hardware noise are identified as open avenues for future work. Appendices restore physical units, derive the scheme's Zitterbewegung in closed form and compare it with a trapped-ion simulation, and execute a reduced two-site instance on a Rigetti superconducting processor, where choosing the qubits from the live calibration lowers the state-preparation error. All operators, circuits, and figures are reproducible from the open-source quantumKineticMethods library.
item.dc:creator: Nilesh Sawant, Ethan Young, Kevin Patrick Griffin, Michael Martin

item.title: Optimal concentration and gradient sensing by perfect monitors
item.description: arXiv:2608.08816v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Cells often estimate chemical concentrations from only a few diffusing molecules, whose stochastic motion limits sensing precision. We consider a perfect monitoring instrument that records the instantaneous molecular density throughout a finite region without perturbing the concentration field or distinguishing molecular identities. The standard Berg-Purcell estimator weights all positions uniformly. Here we derive the optimal spatial weighting within a large class of unbiased estimators for both concentration and gradient sensing. Variance minimization maps to an electrostatic problem. Surprisingly, although the instrument monitors the entire volume, the optimal estimator assigns all weight to its boundary, reducing the uncertainty in both concentration and gradient sensing. We extend the results to arbitrary geometries and spatial dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Farshid Jafarpour

item.title: Categorification of the genus two DAHA
item.description: arXiv:2608.13278v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct three derived endofunctors on the derived category of graded integrable representations of the current algebra of a flat degeneration of $D(2|1,\alpha)$, and prove that their classes in the Grothendieck group are the genus two Macdonald operators. Computing the graded $\operatorname{Ext}$ pairing explicitly, we deduce the self-adjointness of the genus two Macdonald operators and the orthogonality of genus $2$ Macdonald polynomials with respect to the certain skew-bilinear form.
item.dc:creator: Semeon Arthamonov, Ievgen Makedonskyi, Daniil Sarafannikov

item.title: Families of relative periodic orbits in the planar three-body problem via consecutive alignments
item.description: arXiv:2609.01585v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Relative periodic orbits (RPOs) are solutions of the three-body problem that are periodic in a uniformly rotating reference frame and, in general, quasi-periodic in inertial coordinates. We present a numerical procedure for computing and continuing one-parameter families of RPOs of the planar Newtonian three-body problem. The method exploits consecutive syzygies, understood here as configurations in which the three bodies are aligned and their velocities satisfy the corresponding symmetry conditions. Matching the positions and momenta at two consecutive alignments reduces the computation of RPOs to a low-dimensional nonlinear problem. Its solutions are then numerically continued, and linear stability is determined from the nontrivial eigenvalues of the rotated monodromy matrix after removing the neutral directions associated with conserved quantities and continuous symmetries. The procedure is applied to several mass distributions and initial configurations, producing families of Poincar\'e, Hill, and binary-type solutions. These families exhibit transitions from nearly circular to highly eccentric motion, changes of stability near resonances and turning points, and absolute periodic solutions when the rotation angle is a rational multiple of 2{\pi}. In the Hill families, the continuation connects satellite configurations with circumstellar motion as the smallest body loses its gravitational binding to the intermediate body. Circumbinary and circumstellar configurations are also obtained in the binary regime. The results illustrate the dynamical diversity of RPOs and provide coherent three-body motions that can be used as prescribed trajectories in restricted four-body models.
item.dc:creator: Joan Gimeno, Marc Jorba-Cusc\'o, Bego\~na Nicol\'as

item.title: Fully fractional Schr\"odinger equations with memory: well-posedness via extension
item.description: arXiv:2609.01826v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with memory $\Le^s u=\mu|u|^{p-1}u$ for $t>0$, where $\Le^s=(\partial_t-i\Delta_x)^s$, $0<s<1$, and the solution is prescribed for all $t\le0$. We identify a Hilbert space of histories and prove local well-posedness for $1<p\le p_*(s)=1+4s/(d+2-2s)$, with global solutions for sufficiently small histories at the critical exponent. We also establish the passage from this memory problem to the classical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation as $s\uparrow1$. For every fixed Schwartz history and $1<p\le1+4/d$, including the classical mass critical exponent, the memory solutions converge in $C([0,T];L^2\cap L^{p+1})$ to the classical solution with initial value $u_0(\cdot,0)$, for every finite $T$ below its maximal existence time. Thus the limiting evolution depends on the prescribed past only through its value at time zero. Our construction uses an oscillatory Poisson extension and an exact identity expressing the weighted $L^2$ norm of the lifted initial datum in terms of the history. This identity allows us to apply the boundary estimates of our earlier work to the memory problem. We recover $\Le^s$ as a weighted Dirichlet-to-Neumann map and establish the corresponding extension bounds on $L^2$ for $0<s\le\frac12$, and from $\operatorname{Dom}(\Le^s)$ to $L^2$ for $\frac12<s<1$.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Garofalo, Gigliola Staffilani

item.title: Spectral Analysis Beyond the Spectral Gap: Rapid Mixing of Quantum Gibbs Samplers in One Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.05848v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove rapid mixing of a quantum Gibbs sampler for general one-dimensional non-commuting local spin systems at every fixed positive temperature. In particular, for a system of $n$ sites, we show that the Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) detailed-balanced Gibbs sampler of~\cite{CKG2023} converges from any initial state to trace-norm error $\epsilon$ in time $O(\log^4(n)+\log(1/\epsilon))$. This improves the previous $O(n+\log(1/\epsilon))$ bound and establishes rapid mixing beyond high-temperature and weak-interaction regimes. Our proof explains why the slowest decay rate, captured by the spectral gap, can substantially underestimate the speed of equilibration. The key insight is that a state far from equilibrium must have a substantial component outside the span of low-weight Pauli operators, where stronger dissipation estimates apply. This yields two stages of relaxation: a double-exponential convergence from a bad initial state, followed by exponential convergence near equilibrium. We turn this mechanism into a framework for proving rapid mixing through spectral analysis beyond the gap. Our decay estimate is equivalent to exponential convergence in sandwiched R\'enyi-2 divergence. Together with the spectral gap, it also implies a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality with rate $\Omega(\log^{-4}(n))$.
item.dc:creator: Hongrui Chen, Zhiyan Ding

item.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
item.description: arXiv:2610.15006v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a magma-operad (non-associative partial combination, restricted to the image of disintegration) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding on admissible inputs. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---it defines a renormalization operator $R_{\mathcal{I}}=\text{Combine}\circ\text{Disintegrate}$. The information loss of this operator is exactly the probability curvature $\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{I}}(\mu)$---the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This curvature measures the obstruction to lossless decomposition and reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by CDF-based scalar block summaries.
item.dc:creator: Xuexing Lu

item.title: A first order nonabelian antisymmetric tensor model with hidden higher symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.16250v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a nonabelian complex self-dual antisymmetric tensor model, with gauged internal symmetry, comprising a complex multiplet of massless self-dual antisymmetric tensor fields and its conjugate (interacting with massless Yang-Mills gauge fields). We build the model at the classical level, via a first order formulation, assigning local fields to a component expansion over the Dirac algebra and a basis of internal matrices, with Lorentz and gauge invariance ensured by tracing, and applying an appropriate bilinear form. The full expansion requires auxiliary place-holder fields, which are not potentials, but become curvatures (field strengths) after elimination via their algebraic equations of motion. The component expansion over the Dirac algebra is closed under multiplication by additional internal matrices, which are not gauge group generators, but mix internal components, and link auxiliary curvatures with potentials. The model is shown to be invariant under such transformations, and thus possesses a type of hidden internal symmetry. We analyze the specific case of gauge group $SU(2)\! \times \! U(1)$, and as higher symmetry candidates, we consider both the Lie group $SU(3)$ and the Lie superalgebra $SU(2/1)$ (with the additional matrices acting via Lie brackets, or graded Lie brackets, respectively).
item.dc:creator: Peter D. Jarvis, Jean Thierry-Mieg

item.title: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
item.description: arXiv:2610.16351v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An isolated quantum system evolves reversibly, yet a small subsystem can lose nearly all information about its initial state. Conserved quantities may retain some of this information, depending on how strongly they overlap with local observables. Here we consider a subsystem in an arbitrary initial state coupled to a maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square equilibration error, maximised over window origins, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation, with the stationary part subtracted. The two mean-square quantities are linearly comparable. A correlation record over a finite interval therefore controls the equilibration error in every interval of the same length, and the result extends to nonnegative observation weights with nonnegative Fourier transform. The result allows arbitrary degeneracies of energies and gaps. We apply it to two static Hamiltonian families. For fixed spin subsystems in the one-particle sector of a bounded-range periodic clock, fixed-accuracy thermalisation is guaranteed on windows that grow only slightly faster than linearly with system size, despite exponentially small positive energies. A random commuting model with logarithmic interaction range retains an extensive set of conserved observables. Its expected mean-square error is bounded by a finite-size term and an inverse-time term. The inverse-time dependence is unavoidable because of the initial transient. These examples show how local relaxation can coexist with exact conservation laws and a finely spaced spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Piotr \'Cwikli\'nski

item.title: Self-organizing reinforcement learning: a learner-free swarm approaches the explore-exploit optimum
item.description: arXiv:2610.25113v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The explore/exploit trade-off is the core problem of reinforcement learning (RL). We show that a minimal foraging swarm approaches its optimum - the ideal-free / Nash allocation of a multi-agent resource-sharing game (an equilibrium, not a return maximum) - with no learner and no reward signal. Agents explore by heavy-tailed (Levy) flights, recruit neighbours to a discovery through a threshold cascade on their proximity network, and disperse as a patch crowds; this cascade cycle balances exploration and exploitation and drives foragers toward the ideal free distribution. The swarm attains the shape of this optimum (committed foragers track richness with slope 0.94) but not its exact equilibrium - it stays measurably exploitable - reaching it dynamically (~150 steps) through the coupling of recruitment to movement: remove the coupling and matching collapses (0.94 -> 0.08). The RL sits at the level of the problem and the allocation reached, not the micro-rule: no step evaluates payoff (reward-free by construction, though the crowd signal is informationally tied to payoff), and the swarm reaches the allocation without learning it (quality plateaus and re-settles after resources move, no cumulative gain). Against a trained baseline the comparison is two-sided: in an easier, disembodied game a learner is more precise, while in the same embodied environment the reward-free swarm reaches ~65% of a validated oracle ceiling at zero training and leads until trained PPO and centralised-critic (CTDE) learners overtake it (~74-75%, 16 seeds, all above the swarm mean) after ~4,000 of 15,000 training steps - its advantage is in budget, not asymptote. In this one setting we read it not as beating RL but as a strong zero-shot, reward-free operating point: a demonstration that the self-organizing physics of a minimal swarm can carry a collective close to the optimum RL seeks, with none of RL's machinery.

item.title: Nonlocal Equations on Domains and Manifolds Without Symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2610.28572v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we establish existence and regularity results for solutions to nonlinear nonlocal equations of the form $f(\Delta)u = U(x,u)$ and $f(\Delta_{g})u = U(x,u)$ in Euclidean and Riemannian settings, respectively. We prove existence results across three distinct geometric scenarios: bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, perturbed equations on compact Riemannian manifolds, and noncompact Cartan-Hadamard manifolds under suitable geometric curvature conditions.
